extracted.intended_audience: reporters, editors and producers working on news about violence, crisis and trauma
extracted.subtask_description: A concise, evidence-informed style guide for journalists and newsroom decision-makers on reporting trauma, covering language, ethics, science, and special-topic considerations (e.g., sexual violence, racism). Designed for quick reference under deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline literacy in trauma concepts and emerging reporting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: "Responsible reporting and newsroom decision-making now demand baseline literacy in trauma concepts and emerging reporting standards."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies across breaking news, investigative reporting, local beats, international coverage, features and photographs — reporters must have basic knowledge of how violence, abuse, conflict and chronic threat affect individuals, communities and reporting choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-informed guidance on news choices, language usage and ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: The guide "includes brief evidence-informed guidance on news choices, language usage and ethics in reporting on the impact of trauma on individuals, families and communities."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use recommendations grounded in empirical evidence and expert consensus to inform what to report, how to frame stories, and which ethical trade-offs apply in trauma coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of psychological and scientific terminology (e.g., PTSD)
rubrics_metrics.description: The guide recommends "appropriate use of relevant psychological and scientific terminology" and notes areas where guidance is stringent, for instance "the limited circumstances in which it is accurate to refer to Post Traumatic Stress Disorder."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid casual or incorrect application of clinical diagnostic terms; reserve diagnostic language for circumstances supported by evidence or clinical assessment, and clarify uncertainty when using scientific terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special considerations for reporting on racism and sexual violence
rubrics_metrics.description: The guide highlights "special considerations when reporting on consequential trauma-laden issues such as racism and sexual violence."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply heightened ethical, language and sourcing practices when covering topics with additional harm dynamics—consider survivor safety, retraumatization risks, power dynamics, stigma, and community impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish evidence-based consensus from unresolved knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries "rooted in trauma science are grounded in evidence-based consensus among experts, or define fundamental conceptual arguments and other areas of unresolved knowledge."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting, indicate clearly whether guidance is based on well-established science or on contested/uncertain areas; avoid overstating scientific certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize trauma-informed critical thinking over rigid rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors "have emphasized guidelines and recommendations over rigid commandments, recognizing the fluid, complex and assignment-specific nature of journalistic decision-making."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the guide as a flexible tool; apply context-sensitive judgement rather than mechanical rule-following. Encourage newsroom discussion of trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quick, authoritative reference for tight deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The guide is "designed as a quick, authoritative reference for reporters, editors and producers working on tight deadlines."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries are concise and organized for rapid consultation; use them to make fast, informed editorial decisions while preserving core trauma-informed principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Living document: regular updates to reflect evolving best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The Dart Style Guide "is a living document, designed to be regularly expanded and updated to reflect evolving best practices, innovations in news coverage and growing scientific understanding."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect and incorporate updates; treat recommendations as provisional and subject to refinement as research and practice evolve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide links to in-depth resources for further learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries "link to the Dart Center’s extensive online library of tip sheets, backgrounders and journalist-to-journalist guidance, and as well as other authoritative resources."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the guide as a gateway: follow linked deeper resources for complex assignments, training, or detailed clinical/scientific explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider cross-cultural and intersectional perspectives; acknowledge limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The guide states it "attempts wherever possible to reflect global, cross-cultural and intersectional perspectives," while acknowledging the authors are Anglophone and U.S.-based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt guidance to local cultural contexts and identity-based differences; be transparent about cultural limitations of recommendations and seek local expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend to journalists' personal capacity and vicarious trauma
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting on trauma "poses a profound daily challenge to craft and to the personal capacity of news professionals."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include considerations for reporter wellbeing, vicarious trauma and newsroom supports (e.g., peer support, supervision, workload management) when planning and assigning trauma coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt trauma-informed innovations in interviewing, sourcing, investigation and storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists have "forged significant innovations... fresh approaches to interviewing and source development, investigative method, storytelling, ethics and the news agenda itself."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use trauma-aware interviewing techniques, thoughtful source development, ethically informed investigative methods, and storytelling choices that reduce harm and center context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize guidance thematically and alphabetically for rapid lookup
rubrics_metrics.description: The guide is organized in four thematic sections (Trauma Science and Psychology; Violence and Aftermath; Identity; Community and Social Issues) and entries within each section are alphabetical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When consulting the guide, use thematic sections or browser FIND to locate specific terms (e.g., Complex PTSD, childhood trauma).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invite feedback and community input; be transparent about authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: The guide welcomes "feedback, suggestions and criticism" and notes initial compilation and review processes and contact details for comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsrooms and practitioners are encouraged to contribute corrections, context-specific insights, and lived-experience perspectives to improve applicability and accuracy.
